correctness.rationale: The squared incident spin sum gives the local exchange term including its constant. At fixed K a discrete convex exchange of one unit between unbalanced incident counts strictly lowers the shore cost. Both floor/ceiling minima are attainable: put K/N on each base edge in a circulation with the stated degree bounds and the return arc fixed at K. Integrality produces a valid selection; this also handles K=0,N. With positive couplings the difference E_{K+1}−E_K changes sign at h=H_K and H_K jumps exactly at interior multiples of m or n. The intersection has gcd(r,s)−1 interior multiples, and equality gives coexistence along an entire run of equal thresholds. At saturation the flip energy is exactly the sum of positive pair penalties with weights 4J_U,4J_W, so it vanishes precisely on matchings. Independently enumerated by a left-vertex dynamic program with a used-right mask, the size counts for shifts {0,1,2} are (1,18,117,336,420,192,20) and for {0,1,3} are (1,18,117,336,417,186,17), totaling 1104 and 1092. The shifts 0,1 alone form a spanning cycle in each graph.

originality.rationale: The substantial overlap is the exact rook-graph solution, including its balancing method, and known saturation matching descriptions; neither is credited as new. The supported distinction is the uniform fixed-K result for arbitrary biregular bipartite supports with two positive couplings, and realizable distinct matching counts at the same degrees and partition sizes. The close catalogue and primary statements examined do not cover this combination. No priority is inferred from the date of the rook result.
residual_risks: The review does not certify literature priority. The cited de Werra full text was inaccessible; exact balancing principles may exist in stronger form, and related physics literature was not exhausted.

value.rationale: The natural class of biregular supports allows an exact separation of two observables: the spectrum of minimal energies at fixed magnetization is entirely determined by degrees and shore sizes, whereas the saturation ground-state count can resolve incidence differences even among connected bases. The complete sector result and a verified witness pair make the separation usable beyond a special-lattice calculation.
residual_risks: Value is confined to the stated zero-temperature classical model. No general formula for coexistence multiplicities away from saturation is established.
